summary: A chaotic real-time game where you first scramble to slap together a spaceship from randomly drawn tiles under a running timer, then fly it through a gauntlet of meteors, pirates, and disasters hoping the shoddy build holds together. It's equal parts building-phase panic and flight-phase schadenfreude as ships lose engines, cargo, and crew piece by piece.
praised: huge replayability from random tiles and event decks
tension between greedy building and safe building
great for groups who enjoy laughing at their own disasters
criticised: heavy luck in what tiles you draw and what events hit
real-time segment stresses out some players
a ship can be crippled early with little to be done about it
less satisfying for players who want tight strategic control

interaction.detail: During ship-building, all players grab tiles simultaneously from one common pile, so speed and blocking of desired pieces matters directly. During the flight phase, ships share a single track where position determines who meets hazards first and who can be shot at or bumped by others' fire, though most dangers come from the game's event cards rather than direct player actions.

subsystems: build-and-fly integrated ship engine (building feeds directly into the flight survival phase)
sources: cargo sold at end of each flight
penalties for lost/destroyed components and crew
scoring.how_you_win: Build the best ship you can under time pressure, then survive three increasingly dangerous flights; the player with the most credits from cargo sales and encounters, minus losses, wins.
